E:\\Nikith_Projects\\datasets\\fitzpatri.description: This image shows a small, raised, reddish growth on the skin that may bleed easily with minor trauma. It is a type of vascular lesion consisting of an overgrowth of tiny blood vessels, often developing after a minor injury.
E:\\Nikith_Projects\\datasets\\fitzpatri.harm_reason: While benign, it typically will not resolve on its own and tends to bleed easily or become irritated, meaning it should be evaluated and treated by a doctor.

E:\\Nikith_Projects\\datasets\\fitzpatri.description: This image shows severe inflammation, redness, and blistering on the lips, leading to raw erosions and crusting. It is often associated with a serious reaction to medications or an infection that affects mucous membranes. This is a medical emergency that requires immediate professional evaluation and hospital care.
E:\\Nikith_Projects\\datasets\\fitzpatri.harm_reason: This is a serious condition that can cause extensive tissue damage, severe pain, and life-threatening complications if not treated urgently.

E:\\Nikith_Projects\\datasets\\dermnet\\.description: The image shows numerous small, reddish-purple spots spread across the legs, particularly around the knees. These spots represent inflammation and tiny bleeding points within the blood vessels in the skin, which can be caused by various systemic processes or immune reactions.
E:\\Nikith_Projects\\datasets\\dermnet\\.harm_reason: Vasculitis requires medical evaluation because it can be a sign of underlying systemic inflammation or organ involvement that needs professional management.

E:\\Nikith_Projects\\datasets\\mpox-skin.description: The image shows small, clustered spots inside the mouth, which commonly appear as early-stage cold sores or canker sores. These lesions are typically caused by common viral activity in the oral mucosa and often resolve on their own within a week or two.
E:\\Nikith_Projects\\datasets\\mpox-skin.harm_reason: While uncomfortable and potentially recurrent, these viral lesions are generally self-limiting and resolve without permanent harm.

E:\\Nikith_Projects\\datasets\\dermnet\\.description: This image shows rough, thickened skin on the foot containing small dark dots, which are tiny clotted blood vessels. These are plantar warts, caused by a common viral infection of the outer layer of skin. They are typically harmless and often resolve on their own over time, though they can sometimes cause discomfort when walking.
E:\\Nikith_Projects\\datasets\\dermnet\\.harm_reason: Plantar warts are benign viral growths that usually pose no serious health risk and often go away without treatment.

E:\\Nikith_Projects\\datasets\\dermnet\\.description: The image shows grouped small blisters and redness around the cuticle and nail fold of a finger. This presentation is often associated with a viral infection of the finger caused by the herpes simplex virus. It can be sensitive, tingling, or uncomfortable while the blisters heal.
E:\\Nikith_Projects\\datasets\\dermnet\\.harm_reason: It can be painful and tends to recur, so it should be evaluated by a healthcare professional for appropriate management.

E:\\Nikith_Projects\\datasets\\dermnet\\.description: The image shows a prominent, firm, dark-colored nodular growth with central crusting or ulceration located on a finger joint. This presentation can sometimes represent a type of skin cancer, such as a squamous cell carcinoma that has developed a thickened, hyperkeratotic surface. A doctor should examine this growth closely to determine its true nature.
E:\\Nikith_Projects\\datasets\\dermnet\\.harm_reason: Skin cancers can grow, cause local tissue destruction, and potentially spread if they are not evaluated and treated promptly.
